# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.

# Single machine-wide downtime leader across all worklogs (replace per-worklog elections) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Downtime leadership is **per-worklog** (`coordinationDir: join(targetCwd, '.worklog')`): every open project tab runs its own election, lease/lock, and `downtime-coordination.json`. The refactor WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §Multi-worklog support describe a leader that "compares offers across directories" — but no instance ever sees another worklog's offers, so that behaviour does not exist. Result: N independent leaders poll the same shared llama-proxy, oversubscribe its slot budget, and each provide only ~1 item/hour throughput while zombie leases compound divergence.

## Users

- **Herdr users with multiple project tabs open** — want a single machine-wide downtime dispatch queue so idle LLM capacity is shared fairly and not oversubscribed when two projects are idle simultaneously.
  - *Story:* As a user with TCE + ContextHub tabs open, I want the downtime leader to dispatch the globally highest-priority offer (e.g. ContextHub audit before TCE intake) and respect a single slot budget, so two projects never launch 2-slot audits at once.
- **Operators observing downtime logs** — want one coordination file, one lease, one dispatch log to inspect, instead of per-worklog fragments.
- **Agents dispatched via downtime** — benefit from higher global throughput (no per-project 1h cooldown starvation) and correct cross-project tier ordering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — One shared coordination dir:** A second herdr instance opened on a *different* worklog joins the same coordination file; the file contains entries with different `worklogRoot`s.
- [ ] **AC2 — Exactly one leader machine-wide:** With N instances across P worklogs, only one holds a valid lease and no two instances dispatch in the same tick window (tested for the zombie case WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD).
- [ ] **AC3 — Cross-directory tier dispatch:** Leader orders offers by existing tier priority (audit → critical-first → implement → plan → intake) *across* worklog roots and spawns the pane in the entry's `worklogRoot`.
- [ ] **AC4 — Global slot budget:** With 3 proxy slots and 2 projects offering work, total concurrently dispatched/requesting work never exceeds the shared budget (no cross-project oversubscription).
- [ ] **AC5 — Safe migration:** Existing per-worklog coordination files stop being written once the machine dir is authoritative; no double-dispatch during transition; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` updated to match actual behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & build green:** Headless tests prove AC1–AC4 invariants; full herdr test suite + `npm run build` green.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` downtime section, and code comments reflect the machine-wide design; CHANGELOG excluded (ship skill owns it).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- Must land after WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 (cooldown stall) and WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (zombie lease) — both now `completed` (blocked-by satisfied).
- Coordinate with WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (bounded concurrent dispatches) on the machine slot budget — single budget, not per-project.
- Single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) out of scope.
- File-lock + lease model reused from `leader-election.ts`; machine dir default `~/.herdr/downtime/` with `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` env override.
- Fail-safe: unreadable/missing coordination or lease files degrade to "no dispatch this cycle", never crash or drop another instance's entry.
- Must not double-dispatch during migration (a TCE instance with an old TCE file must not ALSO join the machine file with different `instanceId`).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` reads/writes `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-coordination.json` with per-instance `{instanceId, workItemId, directory, assignedAt, lastUpdated}`.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` manages file lock + 5-min lease per worklog.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `createDowntimeWorker` wires `coordinationDir: join(targetCwd, '.worklog')` — the per-worklog coupling to replace.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` describes aspirational multi-worklog behaviour and per-worklog file paths.
- Related fixes landed: zombie lease fix, cooldown probe-before-pause, per-tick re-derivation.

## Desired change

- Introduce **machine-scoped coordination dir** (default `~/.herdr/downtime/`, env override `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR`) containing `coordination.json`, `leader-lease.json`, `leader.lock`, `dispatches.log` (or equivalent names).
- All instances read/write the **same** coordination + lease/lock files regardless of project; each entry carries `worklogRoot` (today's `directory` field, renamed or retained).
- **One election, one lease** machine-wide (reuse `leader-election.ts` against the machine dir); lease survives no-candidate cooldowns (depends on zombie fix — done).
- **Leader dispatches across directories** by tier priority, spawning panes into each entry's `worklogRoot` (viaroot `wl` invocation as today); stale-entry pruning and 30-min check-in cadence carry over per instance.
- **Machine slot budget** enforced by the leader against shared proxy status (coordinate with WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q).
- **Migration/fallback:** prefer machine dir when authoritative; retire legacy `.worklog/downtime-*` files; document retirement; no double-join.
- Correct `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (and package README) to describe actual behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — Switch coordination file/dir resolution to machine-scoped dir; `worklogRoot` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts` — Point lock/lease at machine dir.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Wire machine dir into `createDowntimeWorker` / `runCoordinationCheckIn` / `dispatchFromCoordination`; migration logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Rolling logs under machine dir or per-worklog (decide).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Pass machine coordination dir into worker wiring.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Correct multi-worklog section, file paths, env override.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update downtime worker overview if it mentions file paths.
- `packages/herdr/tests/*.test.ts` (+ new headless tests for AC1–AC4) — Machine-wide invariants.

## Related work

- **Depends on (completed):** WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 (empty-file cooldown stall), WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (zombie lease) — both `completed`.
- **Coordinate with:** WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q (bounded concurrent dispatches, `in_progress`) — machine slot budget is the shared concern.
- **Parent/supersedes:** WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL (leader election + shared coordination file refactor, `completed`) — this item replaces its per-worklog scope; supersedes the aspirational multi-worklog paragraph of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (WL-0MT76H3Z900908TV completed docs page).
- **Downtime family:** WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (spare-capacity dispatch), WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL etc. — prior cadence/budget context.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Migration double-dispatch:** Mitigation — single machine dir authoritative; legacy files not written once migrated; instanceId stays stable across dirs; test with mixed old/new files.
- **File-lock contention on shared dir:** Mitigation — reuse existing `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` + lease pattern; no new concurrency primitive.
- **Worklog root path stability:** Assumption — `directory`/`worklogRoot` is the worklog root (parent of `.worklog`), not cwd; spawn uses `worklogRoot` for `wl` invocation.
- **Scope creep — multi-machine, audit parallelism, new tier kinds:** Record as separate work items, not in scope.
- **Env override discoverability:** Document `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` in docs and settings/README.

## Open Questions

- None blocking intake — design details (exact file names in machine dir, dispatch log location, migration flag) to be settled in plan.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview required — seed context from work-item description was sufficient to draft the brief. No clarifying questions asked; brief derived from existing ACs, proposed design, and repo search.
- Related docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`.
- Related work items: see Related work section above (search keywords: downtime, leader).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6** – Implement tier end-to-end in herdr downtime worker (completed)
- **WL-0MKRRZ2DN0BRRYJC** – Ship Standalone “Folder Binary” Distribution (No npm install) for Worklog CLI (completed)
- **WL-0MQP4RDG2006LFM9** – Fix ruff lint findings in tests/test_audit_runner_core.py (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt32f90v008uad2, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+265 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0msg7ztc000163fl, 0mst3oj8s0001rol, 0mt32f90v008uad2, ac1, ac3 (+192 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: agents, also, another, audit, audits (+187 more)

# Intake Brief: Fair round-robin work scheduling with priority override (WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V)

## Problem Statement
The `dispatchFromCoordination` leader path in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` selects from the shared coordination file (`downtime-coordination.json`) by iterating entries in file order within each tier. With multiple projects contributing (ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine), this allows the same project to monopolise consecutive dispatch slots. We need globally-fair distribution with an exception for critical-priority items.

## Users

- **Agent — Automated downtime worker (primary):** As a downtime worker I want dispatches to fairly represent all contributing projects, so that no single project starves others of agent attention.
- **Developer / Project owner:** As a developer with work in an unserved project, I want the scheduler to eventually assign my project's candidate even when another project has more frequent offers, so that my backlog makes progress.

### User Stories
- As the downtime dispatcher leader, when entries exist from multiple projects at the same tier, I select the project whose last dispatch (in any tier) is oldest (round-robin), so that projects get a fair share of slots.
- As a project owner with a `critical`-priority offer on file, my next dispatch should bypass round-robin and run immediately (still at its stage-appropriate skill), so that urgent work is not delayed by fairness.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `dispatchFromCoordination` selects across the shared coordination entries in **global cross-project round-robin** order: among equally-eligible (tier-matched, non-critical) entries, the project whose `worklogRoot` was least-recently dispatched (with persistence across leader restarts / cycles) is chosen first. New / unknown roots sort first (never penalised). A single persistent cursor/state per worklog root (e.g. in a JSON file alongside the coordination file) drives the ordering; concurrent leaders do not corrupt the cursor (fail-open).
- [ ] When **any** entry on file is a `critical`-priority open item at a dispatchable stage (`idea` / `intake_complete` / `plan_complete` within caps; stage-appropriate skill), the leader dispatches that critical entry **immediately** ahead of all non-critical entries, regardless of round-robin position. Within the critical subset, selection remains deterministic (existing priority/sortIndex tie-break — one item per project, so round-robin is not needed inside critical).
- [ ] The critical override is **global** (evaluated before any tier loop): a critical in `plan_complete` outranks a non-critical `audit`, and a critical `idea` outranks a non-critical `implement`, matching the intent "jump to the front of the queue". The existing freeze (audit/implement skipped while frozen) and caps (`risk <= Medium && effort <= Medium` for `plan_complete`, including critical) are retained.
- [ ] After a successful dispatch (or a `spawn-failed`/`marker-write-failed` claim that still consumes the entry), the round-robin cursor/state advances to mark that project's `worklogRoot` as most-recently served, so the next dispatch in **any** tier starts from the following project.
- [ ] Existing `downtime-worker` and `coordination` tests still pass, plus new tests prove: (a) with two non-critical entries from different projects at the same tier, consecutive dispatches alternate projects; (b) a newly-arrived critical from project B is dispatched next even though round-robin would choose project A; (c) cursor persists across a simulated leader restart.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints
- Must build on the existing coordination machinery (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` lock + atomic write, `machine-coordination.ts` single machine dir) — no new daemon or external dependency.
- Fail-open on missing/corrupt round-robin state (behaves as if no history — original file order), never throws or starves dispatch.
- No behaviour change to `wl next` / single-project flows; this is strictly the multi-project leader path (`coordinationDir` present).
- Preserve dispatched-marker exclusion and CAS claim ordering already in `dispatchFromCoordination`.
- Each project currently registers at most one offer per cycle, so per-project multiplicity can be treated as one entry per root — design should not break if that grows, but need not optimise for many-per-root.

## Existing State
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchFromCoordination` groups fetched entries by tier (`audit` → `critical` → `implement` → `plan` → `intake`) and iterates each group in file order (`entries` array order). No cross-project fairness: repeated offers from the same root can win every slot when they re-queue quickly.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` provides a per-tier persistent cursor for the *legacy* `selectWithRotation` path (unused in coordination mode); the new requirement is **global, cross-tier** round-robin across `worklogRoot`s.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` manages `downtime-coordination.json` with atomic tmp+rename and an `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` lock (`tryAcquireCoordLock` / `withCoordLock`), and already carries `worklogRoot` per entry; `machine-coordination.ts` makes the file machine-wide.
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-cross-root.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.test.ts`.
- Contributing projects: ContextHub, SorraAgents, AI_Hell, Tableau-Card-Engine (each instance writes one entry via `runCoordinationCheckIn`).

## Desired Change
- Introduce a **global per-project round-robin** ordering for `dispatchFromCoordination`: track last-dispatched `worklogRoot` (persistent JSON alongside the coordination file, e.g. `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`), sort same-tier eligible candidates by "least-recently-served first" before dispatch, and advance the cursor on each consumed entry.
- Promote the **critical override** to a global pre-tier check: re-fetch → if any dispatchable critical exists, dispatch the first critical immediately (respecting freeze/caps), before the tier-ordered round-robin loop.
- Add/extend tests to cover alternating-project fairness, critical jump-ahead, and cursor durability; update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and relevant code comments.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Needs updated `dispatchFromCoordination` + new helpers for global round-robin ordering / cursor advance
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — May gain small helpers or remain unchanged (new state file is separate)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin.ts` — May be reused/extended or a new `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` added for worklogRoot-keyed persistence
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — Reference for machine-dir resolution used by the new state file
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Needs new fair-scheduling test cases
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Needs updated dispatch ordering description (fair scheduling + critical override)

## Related Work
- Parent area: `WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL` (Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election + shared coordination file), `WL-0MTF0KLO10043YAN` (Single machine-wide leader), `WL-0MTII45EP002DWK6` (Cross-directory tier dispatch)
- Preceding round-robin work: `WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6` + `downtime-round-robin.ts` / `downtime-round-robin.test.ts` (per-tier cursor, now superseded by global root-level rotation)
- Tier / dispatch reference: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:COORDINATION_TIER_ORDER`, `classifyItemForDispatch`, `COORDINATION_FILE` / `readCoordinationFile` in `coordination.ts`
- Follow-up opportunity: if per-root multiplicity grows beyond one, consider weighted or deficit round-robin (record as a linked work item, not in scope)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** Cursor file races between leaders → Mitigation: reuse the existing `withCoordLock` / tmp+rename pattern; fail-open when lock is contended.
- **Risk:** New critical items arriving between fetch and dispatch could be missed → Mitigation: critical check happens on the same single fetch pass; subsequent arrivals wait one cycle (acceptable at 30-min check-in cadence).
- **Risk:** Stale-entry pruning removes a root before its round-robin turn → Mitigation: pruned roots drop from ordering automatically; no ghost cursor entries block others.
- **Risk:** Scope creep (e.g. per-entry priority weighting beyond critical) → Mitigation: explicitly out of scope; non-critical priorities are treated as equally round-robined (per operator: one item per project).
- **Assumption:** At most one entry per `worklogRoot` per cycle — holds today; ordering by `worklogRoot` last-served is equivalent to ordering by entry last-served.
- **Assumption:** "Jump to the front" means dispatch before any non-critical regardless of tier, not just within the same tier — confirmed with operator (clarification round: globally, dispatch immediately).
- **Assumption:** Persistence should survive leader restarts and machine reboot → file on disk in the machine coordination dir, not in-memory only.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What constitutes a 'project' for fair scheduling?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project downtime scheduling recently implemented — leader election with one work item per project via the herdr extension. Currently ContextHub, ../SorraAgents, ../AI_Hell, ../Tableau-Card-Engine." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Is this about `wl next` or the coordination dispatch?" — Answer (user): "The multi-project case — nothing to do with `wl next`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "When a project has a critical item, does it jump the queue?" — Answer (user): "yes" (affirmative — critical from any project jumps ahead). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Do non-critical priorities (high/medium/low) matter within round-robin?" — Answer (user): "I believe each project only registers a single work item so this is not important." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Round-robin scope — per-tier or globally?" — Answer (user): "globally" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Critical override granularity — immediate dispatch or just cursor bump?" — Answer (user): "dispatch immediately" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
- Q: "Should the cursor persist across cycles/restarts?" — Answer (user): "persistent" Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01.
data.title: Fair round-robin work scheduling with priority override

## Goal

Add targeted tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or `worklist-inflight.test.ts`) that validate the race condition fix and `doRefresh` coalescing behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Test: background dispatch does not trigger stale immediate fetch** — Simulate a `u p c` chord dispatch (background, `openPane: false`); assert that `doRefresh` is NOT called immediately after `executeResolvedCommand` returns `'dispatched'`.
2. **Test: onExit refresh runs after background command** — After the spawned `wl update` child process exits, assert that `doRefresh(false)` (the `onExit` handler) is called and the list reflects the updated priority.
3. **Test: doRefresh coalescing — trailing refresh when in-flight** — Start a `doRefresh` that is in-flight (simulate `fetchItemsForView` awaiting), trigger a second `doRefresh` (simulating `onExit`); assert the first completes and the second runs as a trailing refresh (not dropped).
4. **Test: doRefresh coalescing — at-most-one trailing** — Trigger three rapid `doRefresh` calls while one is in-flight; assert exactly two fetches total (one in-flight + one trailing), not three or more.
5. **Tests use mocked `fetchItemsForView`** — All tests mock `fetchItemsForView` to control timing and avoid real network/DB latency.
6. **All existing Herdr tests continue to pass** — No regressions in `packages/herdr` test suite.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Add new test cases
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-inflight.test.ts` — Extend existing single-flight tests for trailing behavior
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Source under test ( `doRefresh`, `executeResolvedCommand`, `isWlModifyingCommand`)
